Standalone functions: workflow and parameter templates

Source: vignettes/function-reference.Rmd
function-reference.Rmd

This walkthrough provides complete, editable function calls for an R analysis. Copy the relevant blocks and change their settings for your data. Optional arguments are shown at their defaults, including the first choice for arguments with several allowed values. Required files, column names and objects use example values. The explicit MS and peak parameter lists reproduce the defaults and are passed to the corresponding filters so that your edits take effect.

Code is displayed without execution when this vignette is rendered. The main workflow follows imported → after_blank → after_ms → after_qc → after_peak. Blocks marked Alternative or Optional are separate adaptations, not additional steps to execute automatically. Default settings are templates, not recommendations for every dataset. For a worked analysis with figures, see Orbi: blank and MS filtering. Full argument explanations are linked in each section.

Processing logic

Each filtering function takes a prepared dataset and returns an updated object containing the retained features, removed feature IDs, and filter-specific results.

  • Individual filtering calls follow your chosen order. Pass the result of one step to the next. Each step operates on the features retained by the preceding steps, so changing the order can change the results.
  • Each filtering stage can be applied once per object: blank, MS, QC and peak filtering. To change settings or repeat a stage, start again from the saved object immediately before that stage.
  • mc_run() uses a fixed stage order: blank → MS → QC → peak. Stages set to NULL are skipped.
  • MS subfilters run sequentially in a fixed order: isotopes → adducts → neutral losses → in-source fragments → mispicked ions → ringing/saturated ions. Only selected subfilters run. Their order in the filters vector does not change the processing order.
  • QC and peak criteria are combined within their respective stages. A feature must satisfy every selected criterion. For QC, mode determines how results from the evaluated groups are combined.
  • Plotting uses the stored filtering results. It does not rerun filtering. A stage-specific plot requires that stage to have been applied.
  • Final tables and exports use the current retained features. mc_final_table(), mc_write_table() and mc_export() default to format = "input", restoring the original input-table layout.

1. Prepare the peak table

Reference: mc_prepare().

The bundled table provides a convenient starting point. Replace peak_file with your own CSV path. Inspect the detected sample columns before filtering; with sample_keywords = NULL, numeric columns are selected automatically. Set sample_keywords = c(".mzML", "Peak area") or explicit sample_cols if needed. Supported input types are "mzmine", "generic", "xcms", and "msdial".

library(MetaboCensoR)
peak_file <- system.file(
  "extdata", "orbi_iimn_gnps_quant.csv",
  package = "MetaboCensoR", mustWork = TRUE
)
imported <- mc_prepare(
  data = peak_file,
  type = "mzmine",
  sample_cols = NULL,
  sample_keywords = NULL,
  id_col = NULL,
  mz_col = NULL,
  rt_col = NULL,
  labels = NULL,
  token_sep = "_",
  token_index = 2
)
imported$sample_cols
print(imported)

2. Assign sample groups

Reference: mc_labels_from_metadata(), mc_labels_from_names(), mc_labels_from_csv().

Choose one labeling method. Metadata matching is used in the main workflow. The file and column names below are example inputs, not function defaults.

metadata_file <- system.file(
  "extdata", "metadata.csv", package = "MetaboCensoR", mustWork = TRUE
)
imported$labels <- mc_labels_from_metadata(
  path = metadata_file,
  sample_names = imported$sample_cols,
  sample_col = "Sample name",
  label_col = "Label",
  clean_names = FALSE,
  remove_suffixes = NULL
)
data.frame(sample = imported$sample_cols, group = unname(imported$labels))
table(imported$labels)

Alternative: extract groups from sample names.

imported$labels <- mc_labels_from_names(
  sample_names = imported$sample_cols,
  separator = "_",
  token = 2
)

Alternative: read an ordered label CSV. Labels must follow the sample-column order.

imported$labels <- mc_labels_from_csv(
  path = "Label.csv",
  sample_names = imported$sample_cols
)

3. Remove blank-associated features

Reference: mc_filter_blank(), mc_plot_blank().

groups is required: replace "Blank" with your blank group name(s). The default compares mean blank intensity against biological-group means. Use mode = "drop_detected" for the alternative detection-based rule.

after_blank <- mc_filter_blank(
  x = imported,
  groups = "Blank",
  mode = "mean_cutoff",
  cutoff = 0.10,
  labels = NULL
)
mc_plot_blank(x = after_blank, interactive = TRUE)
head(after_blank$blank_tbl)
head(after_blank$removed_ids$blank)

The plot and blank_tbl show saved comparisons. removed_ids$blank identifies features removed at this stage. For static plots, change interactive to FALSE.

4. Configure and apply MS filtering

Reference: mc_ms_parameters(), mc_filter_ms(), mc_plot_ms(), mc_read_mgf().

Complete MS parameter template

All settings below are defaults. RT tolerances are in minutes. Each subfilter uses only the mass tolerance selected by its "da"/"ppm" setting. Set add_pol2 and nl_pol2 separately for negative-mode analyses. With filters = NULL, the enable flags select subfilters; by default only isotopes and adducts are enabled. An explicit filter vector overrides these flags.

ms_options <- mc_ms_parameters(

  # ISOTOPE FILTERING
  enable_iso2 = TRUE,
  iso_cor2 = 0.8,
  iso_rt2 = 0.01,
  iso_tol_type2 = "da",
  iso_mz_tol2 = 0.005,
  iso_ppm2 = 10,
  iso_zmax2 = 3,
  iso_n2 = 1,
  iso_nd2 = 3,

  # ADDUCT FILTERING
  enable_add2 = TRUE,
  add_pol2 = "positive",
  add_cor2 = 0.8,
  add_rt2 = 0.005,
  add_tol_type2 = "da",
  add_mz_tol2 = 0.005,
  add_ppm2 = 10,
  add_min_nm2 = 50,
  add_strict_rt2 = TRUE,
  add_prefer2 = FALSE,
  add_preferred2 = NULL,
  add_prefer_pct2 = 10,

  # NEUTRAL-LOSS FILTERING
  enable_nl2 = FALSE,
  nl_pol2 = "positive",
  nl_cor2 = 0.95,
  nl_rt2 = 0.002,
  nl_tol_type2 = "da",
  nl_mz_tol2 = 0.005,
  nl_ppm2 = 10,

  # IN-SOURCE FRAGMENT FILTERING
  enable_isf2 = FALSE,
  isf_cor2 = 0.95,
  isf_rt2 = 0.01,
  isf_control_int2 = TRUE,
  isf_ratio_min2 = 0.001,
  isf_ratio_max2 = 2.5,
  isf_ms2_check2 = TRUE,
  isf_ms2_rel2 = 1,
  isf_ms2_mz_tol2 = 0.01,
  isf_mgf_id_field = "acquisitionNum",

  # MISPICKED-ION FILTERING
  enable_mis2 = FALSE,
  mis_cor2 = 0.8,
  mis_rt2 = 0.002,
  mis_tol_type2 = "ppm",
  mis_mz_tol2 = 0.005,
  mis_ppm2 = 10,

  # RINGING/SATURATED-ION FILTERING
  enable_ring2 = FALSE,
  ring_cor2 = 0.8,
  ring_rt2 = 0.05,
  ring_tol_type2 = "da",
  ring_mz_tol2 = 0.95,
  ring_ppm2 = 500,
  ring_min_anch2 = 1e+05,
  ring_ratio2 = 10,
  ring_bidirectional2 = FALSE
)

Apply MS filters

The ms_options list above has the same values as the default mc_ms_parameters() call. Passing it explicitly makes the template editable.

after_ms <- mc_filter_ms(
  x = after_blank,
  filters = NULL,
  parameters = ms_options,
  adducts = NULL,
  neutral_losses = NULL,
  spectra = NULL
)

To select filters explicitly, replace filters = NULL with, for example, filters = c("isotopes", "adducts", "isf"). ISF requires spectra when isf_ms2_check2 = TRUE. Optional: read an MGF before the call above and change spectra = NULL to spectra = spectra. Match the MGF feature-ID field to your data. For MS1-only ISF, change isf_ms2_check2 to FALSE in the parameter template. Custom adduct and neutral-loss CSV paths or data frames replace their respective NULL arguments; see Reference for their required columns.

spectra <- mc_read_mgf(path = "your_spectra.mgf")

Inspect MS results

Annotation tables describe inferred ion relationships. A table can be NULL when its subfilter was not run. These assignments support redundancy reduction and do not by themselves establish compound identity.

mc_plot_ms(x = after_ms, interactive = TRUE)
after_ms$ms$counts
head(after_ms$removed_ids$ms)

# Isotopes and adducts
head(after_ms$annot_tbls$iso_table)
head(after_ms$annot_tbls$add_table)

# Other subfilters (NULL if not run)
head(after_ms$annot_tbls$nl_table)
head(after_ms$annot_tbls$isf_table)
head(after_ms$annot_tbls$mis_table)
head(after_ms$annot_tbls$ring_table)

5. Apply QC filters

Reference: mc_filter_qc(), mc_plot_qc().

The default filters = character() selects no criteria and removes nothing. To activate QC filtering, edit it to, for example, c("zeros", "rsd"). Available criteria are "zeros", "mean", "rsd", "dratio", and "min". Before enabling them, replace groups = NULL with the intended evaluation groups; NULL includes all groups, potentially including blanks.

group_any requires each metric to pass in at least one group (different groups may satisfy different metrics); group_every requires every selected group to pass each metric; pooled combines the selected samples. Selected metrics are combined with AND. For D-ratio, specify a genuine pooled-QC group in qc_group and biological groups in groups.

after_qc <- mc_filter_qc(
  x = after_ms,
  filters = character(),
  mode = "group_any",
  groups = NULL,
  zero_metric = "count",
  zero_cutoff = 1,
  mean_cutoff = 5000,
  rsd_cutoff = 30,
  min_cutoff = 1000,
  qc_group = NULL,
  dratio_cutoff = 50,
  labels = NULL
)
head(after_qc$qc_tbl)
head(after_qc$removed_ids$qc)

# QC values and plots exist only when criteria were selected.
if (!is.null(after_qc$qc_tbl) && nrow(after_qc$qc_tbl) > 0L) {
  mc_plot_qc(x = after_qc, filters = NULL, interactive = TRUE)
}

qc_tbl contains metric values and decisions. pass is the group-level decision; keep is the group-aggregated decision for that metric. Failures can overlap across metrics, so their counts should not be added to obtain total removed features. With the default zero-count cutoff of 1, a feature must have no zeros; equality fails the zero cutoff, whereas equality passes mean, RSD, minimum and D-ratio cutoffs.

6. Configure and apply peak filtering

Reference: mc_peak_parameters(), mc_filter_peak(), mc_plot_peak().

Complete peak parameter template

No peak filters are selected by default. Set peak_filters, for example to c("mz", "rt"), to activate criteria. Enabled bounds apply only to selected filters. RT is in minutes, RMD in ppm, and AMD in Da.

peak_options <- mc_peak_parameters(

  # Filter selection
  peak_filters = character(),

  # m/z
  mz_min_enable = TRUE,
  mz_max_enable = FALSE,
  peak_mz_min = 200,
  peak_mz_max = 1500,

  # Retention time
  rt_min_enable = TRUE,
  rt_max_enable = FALSE,
  peak_rt_min = 1,
  peak_rt_max = 30,

  # Relative mass defect
  rmd_min_enable = TRUE,
  rmd_max_enable = TRUE,
  peak_rmd_min = -2000,
  peak_rmd_max = 2000,

  # Absolute mass defect
  amd_min_enable = TRUE,
  amd_max_enable = TRUE,
  peak_amd_min = 0,
  peak_amd_max = 0.5,

  # Target matching
  target_peak_action = "remove",
  target_mz_tol_type = "da",
  target_mz_tol_da = 0.005,
  target_mz_tol_ppm = 10,
  target_rt_tol = 0.05
)

Apply peak filters and inspect results 

after_peak <- mc_filter_peak(
  x = after_qc,
  filters = NULL,
  parameters = peak_options,
  targets = NULL,
  target_text = NULL
)
head(after_peak$peak_tbl)
head(after_peak$removed_ids$peak)
head(after_peak$target_matches)

# Plot selected properties, if any; target matching has no scatter plot.
if (any(after_peak$peak$peak_filters %in% c("mz", "rt", "rmd", "amd"))) {
  mc_plot_peak(
    x = after_peak,
    filters = NULL,
    interactive = TRUE,
    webgl = TRUE
  )
}

peak_tbl contains the features entering this stage, property values, per-filter decisions, and the combined keep decision. target_matches contains target matches when applicable. To use targets, select "target" and supply a CSV or data frame in targets (columns mz and rt), or comma-separated rows in target_text. Both m/z and RT tolerances must be satisfied.

Optional: inspect property distributions even with no peak filters selected. This explicitly changes the plotting argument from its default; inactive bounds are not drawn.

mc_plot_peak(
  x = after_peak,
  filters = c("mz", "rt", "rmd", "amd"),
  interactive = TRUE,
  webgl = TRUE
)

7. Summarize and inspect the final result

Reference: mc_summary(), print.metabocensor_result(), mc_plot_summary(), mc_final_table().

final <- after_peak
print(final)
mc_summary(x = final)
mc_plot_summary(x = final, interactive = TRUE)

# Removed feature IDs grouped by filtering stage
final$removed_ids

# Retained table in the original input layout
final_table <- mc_final_table(x = final, format = "input")
head(final_table)
dim(final_table)

Use format = "standard" for Feature ID, mz, rt (minutes), and intensities, or format = "internal" to inspect the internal layout including .FID. Intermediate objects such as after_blank and after_ms can be inspected and exported with the same functions.

Optional: compare settings. Start both alternatives from the same object before the stage. This example changes the blank cutoff deliberately; other arguments retain their defaults.

alternative_blank <- mc_filter_blank(
  x = imported,
  groups = "Blank",
  mode = "mean_cutoff",
  cutoff = 0.20,
  labels = NULL
)
mc_summary(x = after_blank)
mc_summary(x = alternative_blank)
# Features removed at 0.10 but not at 0.20
setdiff(after_blank$removed_ids$blank, alternative_blank$removed_ids$blank)

8. Export tables and matching spectra

Reference: mc_export(), mc_write_table(), mc_filter_mgf(), mc_write_mgf().

Complete export template

By default, mc_export() returns the table without writing files or processing spectra. Replace the NULL arguments to write files or include spectra.

output <- mc_export(
  x = final,
  csv = NULL,
  mgf = NULL,
  mgf_file = NULL,
  id_field = "acquisitionNum",
  match_col = NULL,
  format = "input"
)
head(output$table)

Optional: write the table and matching MGF together. This is an adaptation of the default template. It requires spectra from the MGF import block and a correct correspondence between feature IDs and id_field.

output_dir <- "MetaboCensoR_results"
dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
output <- mc_export(
  x = final,
  csv = file.path(output_dir, "filtered_table.csv"),
  mgf = spectra,
  mgf_file = file.path(output_dir, "filtered_spectra.mgf"),
  id_field = "acquisitionNum",
  match_col = NULL,
  format = "input"
)
head(output$table)
output$spectra

Alternative: export a CSV only.

mc_write_table(
  x = final,
  path = "filtered_table.csv",
  format = "input"
)

Alternative: subset and write spectra separately.

filtered_spectra <- mc_filter_mgf(
  spectra = spectra,
  table = final,
  match_col = NULL,
  id_field = "acquisitionNum"
)
mc_write_mgf(spectra = filtered_spectra, path = "filtered_spectra.mgf")

Save annotation tables and summaries

These optional base-R exports preserve useful supporting results separately from the final peak table. Empty or unavailable annotation tables are skipped.

output_dir <- "MetaboCensoR_results"
dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
write.csv(mc_summary(x = final),
          file.path(output_dir, "filtering_summary.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
for (nm in names(final$annot_tbls)) {
  tab <- final$annot_tbls[[nm]]
  if (is.data.frame(tab) && nrow(tab) > 0L) {
    write.csv(tab, file.path(output_dir, paste0(nm, ".csv")), row.names = FALSE)
  }
}
for (stage in names(final$removed_ids)) {
  write.csv(data.frame(Feature = final$removed_ids[[stage]]),
            file.path(output_dir, paste0("removed_", stage, ".csv")),
            row.names = FALSE)
}
# Preserve the full result, settings and stored tables for later inspection.
saveRDS(final, file.path(output_dir, "MetaboCensoR_result.rds"))

9. Alternative: run several stages in one call

Reference: mc_run().

The full default template below skips all stages. Replace each NULL with a named list of that filter’s arguments (excluding x). This is an alternative to the separate filtering calls; start from imported again.

after_run <- mc_run(
  x = imported,
  blank = NULL,
  ms = NULL,
  qc = NULL,
  peak = NULL
)

For example, the following adaptation applies blank and MS filtering using the parameter list defined above. QC and peak stages are skipped. Inspect or export after_run with the same functions used for final.

after_run <- mc_run(
  x = imported,
  blank = list(groups = "Blank", mode = "mean_cutoff", cutoff = 0.10,
               labels = NULL),
  ms = list(filters = NULL, parameters = ms_options, adducts = NULL,
            neutral_losses = NULL, spectra = NULL),
  qc = NULL,
  peak = NULL
)
mc_summary(x = after_run)
mc_plot_summary(x = after_run, interactive = TRUE)
